heroHeadline: ROMANIA CONFIRMS GALATI DRONE WAS RUSSIAN GERAN-2; ARTICLE 4 CONSULTATION DISCUSSED; US FORMAL NATO WITHDRAWAL PLAN EXPECTED JUNE; ANKARA SUMMIT 36 DAYS OUT
heroSubtitle: As of June 1, 2026, Romania's official forensic investigation has confirmed the May 28–29 drone strike on a Galati apartment building — the first to cause civilian casualties on NATO territory — was carried out by a Russian-manufactured Geran-2. The Cyrillic stencil 'ГЕРАНЬ-2' was recovered from drone fragments; engine components, navigation systems, and fuel signatures matched known Geran-2 specifications. Russia's May 30 diplomatic deflection — claiming the drone was 'likely Ukrainian' — is eliminated by physical evidence. Romanian President Nicușor Dan formally established 'Russian origin.' NATO and Romania are now formally discussing invoking Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty — a formal convening of the North Atlantic Council to consult on threats to territorial integrity — rather than Article 5 collective defense. The gap between 'every inch' language (Rutte, US Ambassador Whitaker) and the mechanism chosen (Article 4 consultation rather than Article 5 activation) represents the most direct test of alliance credibility in the tracker's nine-year span. Simultaneously, the United States is expected to submit a formalized European force-level withdrawal plan to NATO allies as early as this month — codifying the 10,200+ troop reductions (Germany 5,000, Poland 4,700+500) and the hardware contribution cuts secretly disclosed by Pentagon adviser Velez-Green on May 26 (Der Spiegel): fighter jets available to NATO cut by one-third, strategic bombers halved, zero US submarines contributed, zero US drones. The 'zero US drones' commitment, set against Romania's confirmed Geran-2 strike and its ongoing 28-incursion airspace violation pattern, crystallizes the structural European capability gap that the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8, 36 days away) must address.
